flagged.evidence: https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/pubsub-basics: "When a topic has multiple subscriptions, then every message has to be sent to a subscriber receiving messages on behalf of each subscription." On fan-out it says: "Each of the subscriber applications gets the same set of published messages from the topic." Load balancing (a subset of messages per subscriber) only happens when several subscribers share one subscription.
flagged.problem: The answer (false) and the explanation are correct. However, fan-out compared with load-balanced delivery across subscriptions is message-delivery semantics an engineer configures. That is beyond the CDL objective, which only asks candidates to describe what Pub/Sub is for in modernizing data pipelines. Also, "default subscription" is not a Pub/Sub term (the documented types are pull, push, BigQuery and Cloud Storage subscriptions). Subscriptions with a filter receive only the messages that match it, so an expert could pick at the wording.
flagged.suggestedFix: Drop the card, or replace it with a use-case card such as: "Pub/Sub can deliver the same stream of events to several independent systems, such as analytics and alerting, at the same time." (true).
